title: The Lord on the Throne
summary: Isaiah sees the Lord seated upon a high throne in the temple, with the Lord’s train filling it and seraphim above.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the Lord’s train filled the temple.
Seraphim stood above; each had six wings, covering face and feet with four and flying with two.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The throne is elevated inside the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord’s physical appearance and clothing are not described.
The seraphim’s appearance beyond their six wings is not described.
The temple’s architecture and furnishings are not described.

narration.text: In the year that king Uzziah died

prohibited_inventions: Do not give the Lord an appearance beyond the details stated.

title: The Seraph’s Cry
summary: One seraph cries to another; the doorposts move and smoke fills the temple.

explicit_facts.text: One seraph cried to another, declaring the Lord of Hosts holy and the whole earth full of his glory.
The doorposts moved at the voice of the one who cried, and the house filled with smoke.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Smoke is visible within the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The smoke’s appearance and the temple’s design are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: One seraph

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The earth being full of glory is part of the seraph’s proclamation, not a described visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earth itself visibly filled with glory.

title: Nephi’s Lament
summary: Nephi laments that he is undone, says he has unclean lips and dwells among a people of unclean lips, and says he has seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he is undone and is a man of unclean lips.
Nephi says he dwells among a people of unclean lips.
Nephi says his eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may appear distressed while speaking.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi’s appearance, clothing, posture, and surroundings are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wo is unto me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips; and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied instruction identifies the first-person speaker as Nephi.
His statement that he has seen the King does not establish that the King is visibly present during this speech.
Unclean lips should not be depicted as a physical transformation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the mentioned people as physically present.
Do not stage an appearance of the King, the Lord of Hosts.
Do not invent a location, additional events, or additional dialogue.

title: The Live Coal
summary: One of the seraphim flies to Nephi with a live coal in his hand, previously taken from the altar with tongs. The seraph lays it upon Nephi's mouth and declares that his iniquity is taken away and his sin purged.

explicit_facts.text: One of the seraphim flew to the first-person narrator, identified as Nephi by the supplied instruction, carrying a live coal in his hand.
The seraph had taken the coal from the altar with tongs.
The seraph laid the coal upon the narrator's mouth.
The seraph declared that the coal had touched the narrator's lips, his iniquity was taken away, and his sin purged.

unspecified_visual_details: The encounter's location and the altar's position are unspecified.
The supplied verses describe the seraph flying and having a hand, but provide no further appearance details.
Nephi's appearance and the designs of the altar and tongs are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Lo, this has touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Seraph

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied instruction explicitly identifies the first-person narrator as Nephi; these two verses do not independently name him. The conflicting audit identification as Isaiah is not adopted.
Verse 2 is not supplied and cannot establish appearance details for this scene.
The removal of iniquity and purging of sin are the seraph's declarations, not described visible transformations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a temple setting or establish the encounter's position relative to the altar.
Do not stage the earlier taking of the coal as a simultaneous event.
Do not import wing counts, wing arrangements, or other appearance details from unsupplied verses.
Do not invent additional figures, dialogue, burns, wounds, pain reactions, or visible purification effects.

title: Isaiah Answers
summary: The Lord asks whom to send, and Isaiah offers himself.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah hears the Lord ask whom to send and who will go for them; Isaiah answers, offering himself.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Isaiah remains in the temple while hearing and answering.
unspecified_visual_details: No new appearance of the Lord is described in this verse.

spoken_dialogue.text: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord’s voice is heard; the verse does not specify a new visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent another speaker or a new form for the Lord.

title: A Message to This People
summary: An unidentified speaker instructs someone to tell this people, speaks of hearing without understanding and seeing without perceiving, and then speaks of their hearts, ears, eyes, conversion, and healing.

explicit_facts.text: And he said:
Go and tell this people—Hear ye indeed, but they understood not; and see ye indeed, but they perceived not.

Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes—lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted and be healed.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker and addressee are not identified in the supplied verses.
No location or physical appearance is specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Go and tell this people—Hear ye indeed, but they understood not; and see ye indeed, but they perceived not.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes—lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted and be healed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The language about hearts, ears, and eyes is teaching, not a narrated physical change.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the speaker or addressee, or specify a location, from these verses alone.
Do not depict hearts, ears, or eyes physically changing.

title: How Long?
summary: Nephi asks how long. The Lord answers with a prediction of desolation, removal of men, and forsaking.

explicit_facts.text: Then said I: Lord, how long?
And he said: Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate;
And the Lord have removed men far away, for there shall be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown listening to the answer.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord’s visible appearance is not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: And the Lord have removed men far away, for there shall be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The desolation, removal, and forsaking are described in the answer, not narrated as events occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the predicted desolation or removal as present action.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord or a specific location.

title: The Holy Seed
summary: A tenth is foretold to return and be eaten. A comparison to trees describes the holy seed as the substance thereof.

explicit_facts.text: there shall be a tenth, and they shall return, and shall be eaten,
so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker, setting, and appearance of the tenth and holy seed are unspecified.

narration.text: But yet there shall be a tenth, and they shall return, and shall be eaten, as a teil-tree, and as an oak whose substance is in them when they cast their leaves; so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trees are comparisons, not narrated visible events. The return and being eaten are foretold, not shown happening in this verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not attribute the words to an unidentified speaker or place Isaiah in a temple.
Do not stage the future return or depict a tree consuming people.
